title: Trusting learners' own reports
statement: How far can learners' own reports of what they know be trusted for routing their study?
example: About 80% of students check a word as known, about 50% can give an example and about 20% can explain it.
detail: The diagnostic BrainLift calls self-report the cheapest, fastest and most underused signal in diagnostic assessment, and in a low-stakes mastery setting would use it to set starting estimates that item responses then update (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/WF - Assessment  Feedback Brain - 260624-200115.md`). The reading-science synthesis quotes a 2002 research report finding that most child and adult readers calibrate the success of their comprehension poorly (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/SYNTHESIS.qmd`). The reading BrainLift records far more students checking a word as known than able to explain it (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/teaching-reading-comprehension-brainlift.md`).
